title: Vocal Jazz: battery-in check of the wireless mics at FOH
about: Gameplay slice v2 (PRODUCT_DESIGN.md sections 45, 46, 94 and principle 4.10): the battery-in check at FOH. One signal chain (handheld -> receiver -> X32 input), two faults (batteries in the wrong way round on an early mic; an unpaired 'bad mic' later that gets set aside for a spare), one objective that completes only on verified evidence, one hint ladder, a visible step list, 'Check the rest' after three mics by hand, and one debrief. Everything marked tentative or unknown below is a placeholder to field-calibrate, not room truth.

intro.headline: OH NO!
intro.line: USingers has only left you {minutes} minutes to set up for Vocal Jazz!
brief: {mics} wireless mics, one routine for each: take it from the drawer, batteries in from the charger, switch it on, talk into it at the X32 and watch its meter, then put it on the chair.
Do three by hand. After that, "Check the rest" runs the routine for you and stops on anything that sounds wrong.
A mic that won't work? Find out why before you fix it. Can't fix it? Back in the drawer it goes: a spare covers it.
intro.status: Cary (collaborator), 2026-10-01: a title card on entering the game, with Cary, Morgan and Magnolia saying 'Relax, let's handle this!'. Headline and the crew's line are Cary's; the brief is agent wording (tentative). USingers is the university choir that rehearses in the hall right before Vocal Jazz (Cary, 2026-10-01). {minutes} comes from clock.start/ready_by, {mics} from the mic count.
intro.mentor_status: Cary, 2026-10-02: the player picks one of the three as a mentor; hints come as that mentor's speech bubbles. Cary, 2026-10-08: a separate mentor per level (mics, monitors, line check), each remembered on its own, picked on a card when the level starts. The hint text is the same whoever you pick (no personalities are decided). The line-check brief is agent wording (tentative).
intro.job_status: Cary, 2026-10-08: the mics and the monitors happen at the same time; the A1 and A2 split up. You pick one; the crew covers the other. Both lead into the line check. The monitors brief is agent wording (tentative).
brief_monitors: Three wedges from the storage closet to the stage: lift them (tap fast!), one or two at a time.
The long speakON run from the NX3000's Channel A to the first wedge, then daisy-chain the others. The cables hang on the hook on the Monitor Rack.
Power the Furman, then the NX3000. Then have the A1 play the Wii Shop theme through Bus 1, and listen to every wedge.
intro.level_mentor_prompt: Pick your mentor for this level
brief_line: First the wedges: play the Wii Shop theme through Bus 1 and listen.
Then down the line from black / red: each singer says something while you watch their meter, then tells you if they can hear themselves in the wedge.
You can't touch the mics on stage: ask the singer, or send the A2.

clock.status: tentative: 4:50 doors / 5:00 rehearsal come from PRODUCT_DESIGN section 40. Per-action and per-move seconds are placeholders (section 89: field-calibrate); owner, 2026-09-27: make each check faster for now (was 5 s / 4 s), timing to be adjusted later.

setup.status: owner, 2026-09-27: about 13 musicians, so 13 mics + 2 spares (in case one dies from bad batteries or frequencies) + 1 at FOH for the A1 to talk to the stage through the monitors = 16, on channels 1-16.
setup.note: X32 and receivers start powered on, so the one fault is at the transmitter (one fault per section 94).

roles.value: This slice is the battery-in check at FOH (A2 alone, next to the receivers and the X32), as soon as batteries go into each mic and before the mics go to the stage. The official line check is later, on stage: musicians make sound, the A1 confirms each channel at the X32.

mic_roles.status: owner, 2026-09-27: channels 1-13 are the musicians' mics. 14, 15 and 16 are three interchangeable spares kept at FOH: any of them can be the A1's talkback mic, or the emergency mic the A2 runs down to the stage to replace a dead one. Roles don't change the check yet.

start_state.value: every handheld is in the drawer, switched off, with no batteries; charged cells are in the charger on top of the mic cabinet
start_state.status: owner, 2026-09-28: batteries go in from the charger, then you switch it on

ptu6000-rx.label: Phenyx Pro PTU-6000 receivers
ptu6000-rx.unknown: whether a muted transmitter still shows RF on the receiver. Only audio present / absent is modelled.
ptu6000-rx.units_status: current fact (owner, 2026-09-27): each receiver unit is 8 channels, top unit = 1-8, next = 9-16, and so on

devices_status: Owner, 2026-09-27: mics are named by windscreen colour then ring colour, and that is how people mostly refer to them (black red = 1, black orange = 2, black black = 7, black grey = 8, grey red = 9, grey orange = 10, grey black = 15, grey grey = 16). Ring order (owner-confirmed): red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, black, grey. Mics 17-24: treat as no windscreen for now (owner, 2026-09-27; may change). Handhelds live in the FOH mic drawer (manifest row IMG_4127). State `battery`: "ok" is the only value used in v2; see future_faults. RF group/channel (owner, 2026-09-27): mic N is NOT RF channel N. Each mic has its own group and channel number, which selects a frequency and is set by pairing with its receiver (a procedure of its own). Real values not recorded; the engine draws them from the seed (see rf). For now every mic is assumed paired; an unpaired mic, or any other problem, is simply a 'bad mic' that gets swapped for a spare. Pairing can be a later level.

rf.assignment: seeded, unique per mic; each receiver slot carries the same group/channel as its paired mic

bad.label: Back in the drawer (bad mics)
bad.status: Cary, 2026-10-02: bad mics go back in the drawer. The game still tracks them as set aside (bad), so the spares cover them; how the crew marks a mic as bad in the drawer is not recorded.

connections_status: Current fact (owner, 2026-09-27): handheld N -> receiver channel N -> X32 input N, over handheld -> PTU-6000 -> XLR -> X32 local analog input (PRODUCT_DESIGN section 37). 'Receiver channel N' here means the Nth receiver slot (the owner's earlier answer), not the RF group/channel shown on the mic's display.

faults.label: Batteries in the wrong way round

placement.status: owner, 2026-09-28: 'one of the first few microphones has a fault where you accidentally put in the batteries in the wrong orientation'; 2nd or 3rd per the owner's earlier answer

faults.fix: take the batteries out and put them back the right way round, then switch it on

debrief.failed: the batteries went into {mic} the wrong way round, so it could not switch on.

act.reseat_batteries: you put the batteries back into {mic} the right way round.

debrief.still: {mic}'s batteries are still the wrong way round.
debrief.concepts: no power, no signal: check the batteries before anything downstream

hints.text: It won't switch on, so nothing can reach the receiver. What does a transmitter need before it can power up?
Check the batteries in the handheld.
The batteries are in the wrong way round. Put them back the right way, switch it on, and verify at the X32.

faults.hints_status: tentative: written in the shape of the section 46 ladder (concept, location, direct); for the owner to correct

faults.label: A handheld that is not paired with its receiver

placement.status: tentative: one of the later musician mics (5-13), so it is usually met through Check the rest; the owner's example of a 'bad mic' (2026-09-28): 'if it's not paired or some other problem then it's basically just a bad mic and we'll skip it'

faults.fix: not fixable in this check (pairing is a later level): put it back in the drawer as a bad mic; a spare covers it

debrief.failed: {mic} was not paired with its receiver: it switched on, but its group/channel didn't match its receiver slot, so nothing arrived.

act.put:bad: you put {mic} back in the drawer as a bad mic.

debrief.still: {mic} is still in play, and it will never reach its receiver.
debrief.concepts: a transmitter and its receiver must share a group/channel (pairing); an unfixable mic goes back in the drawer and a spare covers it

hints.text: It's on and not muted, but its receiver hears nothing. What links a transmitter to its receiver?
Compare the group and channel on the mic's display with its receiver slot.
It isn't paired with its receiver, and pairing isn't part of this check. Put it back in the drawer as a bad mic: a spare covers it.

tx-muted.label: A wireless handheld is powered on but muted
tx-muted.note: owner, 2026-09-27: an on-stage line-check fault (a freshly powered mic starts unmuted); kept for the line check scenario
tx-muted.fix: unmute it (tap), or switch it off and on

debrief.failed: {mic} was powered on but muted, so no audio left the transmitter.

act.press:hold: you switched {mic} off and on, which cleared the mute. It works, though a tap would have unmuted it directly.

debrief.concepts: a transmitter can be on but muted

hints.text: No signal is reaching the receiver. Where could the problem be upstream?
The transmitter is muted. Unmute it and verify signal.

objective.label: Battery-in check: the wireless mics
objective.goal: Before the mics go to the stage, verify every one: talking into it shows signal at its X32 input. A mic that can't be fixed goes back in the drawer; a spare covers it.
objective.source: PRODUCT_DESIGN sections 45 (battery-in check; speak into each mic), 55 (goals, not recipes; complete only after verification)

need_verified.status: tentative: every musician needs a working mic (13, setup.mic_roles); the spares 14-16 cover any that are set aside

steps.text: Take the right mic from the drawer: windscreen colour, then ring colour.
Put two batteries in from the charger, the right way round.
At the X32, talk into it: its channel's meter must move.
Put it on the chair left of FOH.

procedure.optional: The mic's display (group/channel, battery, mute) shows while it's in your hand. You don't need it when everything works; it's how you troubleshoot one that doesn't.
procedure.status: owner, 2026-09-28: this is the procedure (grab the right mic by colour, batteries in from the charger, switch it on, check the meter at the X32 = the win criterion).
procedure.bad_mic: Can't make it work, and it isn't the batteries? Put it back in the drawer as a bad mic: a spare covers it.
procedure.display_status: Cary (collaborator), 2026-10-01: show the display as soon as the mic is in hand, instead of a separate 'read the display' action.

skip.label: Check the rest
skip.does: for the remaining mics in channel order, the same routine as by hand, carrying up to two at a time (take them, batteries in, switch on, then at the X32 for each: talk into it, put it on the chair), costing the same game time; set-aside mics are skipped; it stops at the first mic whose X32 input shows no signal, and leaves it (and any unchecked partner) in your hands at the X32
skip.status: PRODUCT_DESIGN 4.10 (owner, 2026-09-27); 3 by hand is from the brief
